Nina: Quick questioncan we carry over PTO into next year? Some folks on my team are saving days for Q1 launches.
Maya (People Ops): Yes, standard policy: up to 40 hours carryover for FT employees (pro-rated for part-time). Anything above that needs manager + People Ops approval; >80h escalates to Director.
Rob: Does sick/vacation separate? And what about international folks?
Maya (People Ops): Sick is separate and handled per local law (some countries require sick carryover). If youre outside the US ping me and we'll confirm local rules.
Sam (Payroll): Accruals post each pay period. High level: `0-1yr: 80h/yr`, `1-3yr: 120h/yr`, `3+yr: 160h/yr`. See full matrix in HRIS > Policies.
Nina: How do people request carryover?
Maya (People Ops): Submit a "Carryover Request" in HRIS Time Off by Jan 15. Manager approves in the system, People Ops reviews any exceptions. We snapshot balances on 2024-12-31 23:59 UTC. Unapproved excess hours will be reduced to cap on Jan 20.
HRIS Bot: Reminder: Edit your time-off entries before snapshot: https://redwoodintranet/hr/pto-policy
Rob: Any blackout dates around holidays/releases I should warn the team about?
Maya (People Ops): Soft blackout for core infra & product: Dec 10-17 (release prep). Company-wide end-of-year freeze Dec 24-31; staggered rotations allowed with manager signoff.
Nina: Emergency unpaid/advanced PTO options?
Maya (People Ops): Managers can approve advance up to 40h for emergencies; People Ops must sign off. Advances get reconciled via future accruals or payroll deduction if needed.
Nina: Great, I'll tell the team to submit by Jan 15 and flag any Dec conflicts now. Thanks!
Maya (People Ops): Thanks  one pager checklist: 1) Submit Carryover Request by Jan 15; 2) Manager approves; 3) People Ops reviews exceptions; 4) Note blackout windows and set approver delegates if OOO. Ping me for edge cases. :calendar:
